names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 30 Οκτωβρίου, «Άγιοι Τέρτιος, Μάρκος, Ιούστος και Αρτεμάς οι Απόστολοι από τους Εβδομήκοντα», with the rank words left off.
The page's second form for the same man: «Ο Ιούστος (ή Ιησούς) έγινε επίσκοπος Ελευθερούπολης», and its epigram for him is headed «Eις τον Iησούν».

Read out of the calendar's own life for the four, «Святой Иуст, называемый Варсавою», which prints the nominative; the day's line declines it, «Иуста», and the name link behind the line is titled with the other of his names, «Святой Варсава, апостол от 70-ти». His own life page is headed «Святой Варсава (Иосиф, Иуст), апостол от 70-ти» and gives all three.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 30. октобар ст. ст., „Св. ап. Клеопа, Терције, Марко, Јуст и Артем.“ — «Св. ап.» is "saint" plus the `apostle` grade, and the other four names are the heading’s other members, so the bare personal name is the whole of the form. The heading gives him no see and no patronymic: «син Јосифа Обручника» and «епископ … у Елевтеропољу» are both in the body, and the see is already the folder’s `office`. `foldchk.py` finds the string on `justus-1-june`, so the form joins a fold of two, keyed in `READ_FOLDS` in the same commit. Four characters exactly, which is the shortest form this block has stored and just inside `nameKeys`’s four-character minimum — one letter shorter and it would not be indexed for folds at all.

feast.note: The Greek calendar keeps the same four apostles on its own 30 October; this is the Russian calendar's own day and not a second day on one calendar. His own life page lists «4 января (70 ап.)», the synaxis of the Seventy, and «30 октября»; one row per church is the schema, so the synaxis is recorded here and he does not render on it.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 30 октября ст. ст. — «Апп. от 70-ти Тертия , Марка , Иуста и Артемы (I).»
source.note: The line is the second of the day. The day carries one typikon sign only, «Cовершается служба, не отмеченная в Типиконе никаким знаком», so no rank is recorded.

attestations.note: That this is the same man the Greek page gave the corpus is read off the see: saint.gr has «Ο Ιούστος (ή Ιησούς) έγινε επίσκοπος Ελευθερούπολης» and the Russian life has «епископствовал и мученически скончался в Елевферополе». The Russian adds the martyrdom, which the Greek page did not have, and a third name and a parentage: he is «Варсава», Barsabas, the son of Joseph the Betrothed, and one of the two put forward in place of Judas Iscariot at Acts 1.23-26. **The calendar names him three ways and the folder stores one.** The day's line prints «Иуста», the name link behind it is titled «Святой Варсава, апостол от 70-ти», and his own life page is headed «Святой Варсава (Иосиф, Иуст)» — Barsabas, Joseph and Justus for one man. The stored form is the nominative «Иуст», which that life page prints in its text, because it is the name the day's line and this folder's display name both use; the other two are recorded here and are not kept as forms, since the calendar gives no way to tell which of the three it would call the fullest. The Greek page's second name for him was «Ιησούς», Jesus, which is none of these three.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (1 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 30ης Οκτωβρίου — «Άγιοι Τέρτιος, Μάρκος, Ιούστος και Αρτεμάς οι Απόστολοι από τους Εβδομήκοντα»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 30 Οκτωβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The entry enumerates four apostles of the Seventy, each with his own see, so it is four folders in principle. The corpus's four other Justuses are none of them this man: Justus of Rome is a martyr with a Greek feast on 28 February, and the others are a soldier, a companion of Matthew, and one kept by date on 1 June. No year, so no `dates` object. No hymn. No asterisk and not the sentence «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη η ύπαρξη του Αγίου».

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 12.11.2025 (30. октобар ст. ст.) — „Св. ап. Клеопа, Терције, Марко, Јуст и Артем.“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, fourth of the five apostles it enumerates. THE HEADING ENUMERATES FIVE APOSTLES — «Клеопа, Терције, Марко, Јуст и Артем» — so the brief’s enumeration ruling makes it one folder per named member, and all five rows quote the whole heading. FOUR of the five take a row here. THE FIFTH, Марко, TAKES NOTHING: `mark-of-byblos` already carries a venerated serbian row out of this same book’s Julian 27 September, where it identifies him in the same words this entry does, and section 1 makes a saint already venerated on another day report-only. The reading is in the commit message. ONE `types` ROW ADDED, READ AND NOT ASSUMED: `martyr`, off «Као епископ пострадао за Јеванђеље у Елевтеропољу» — as bishop he suffered for the Gospel at Eleutheropolis. `hieromartyr` was refused for the same reason as on `tertius`, in the same commit. The folder’s `apostle` and its `office` «Bishop of Eleutheropolis» are confirmed and untouched. `dates` UNTOUCHED: `death` 1 to 100 off the Russian «(I)», and this entry gives no year. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS, AND IT IS A GENEALOGY AND A LOST LOT. HE WAS THE SON OF JOSEPH THE BETROTHED. AND HE WAS THE OTHER CANDIDATE: chosen by lot TOGETHER WITH MATTHIAS for the place of Judas the betrayer, AND REMAINED UNCHOSEN. That is this folder’s own two `related` rows — `joseph-the-betrothed` and `matthias-the-apostle` — stated by a third book, so both rows are confirmed and neither is new, and no row is owed. The new paragraph links both and the reciprocals were checked rather than assumed. No `locations`: Eleutheropolis is named and is already in the `office`. THE FORM FOLDS AND THE FOLD IS KEYED: «Јуст» is already held by `justus-1-june`, a `martyr` of 163 whom doxologia names in a bare line, so this takes the key from one holder to two. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day’s verse is Bishop Nikolai’s own and is about king Milutin.

death.note: days.pravoslavie.ru's line for 30 октября ст. ст. closes the four apostles with «(I)», the first century, and neither of its two lives for him gives a year. The folder held no `dates` before this; saint.gr gave him none.
